title: Prioritized session SLOs and asymmetric burn policy for embeddings inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a session-aware SLO framework and rollout gates for embeddings inference that: (1) supports mixed synchronous and asynchronous workloads, (2) applies per-tenant provisional error budgets with asymmetric burn rates for priority lanes, and (3) defines automated circuit-breaker thresholds and fallback routing rules. This ticket captures PRD-level requirements, acceptance criteria, contract tests, and the phased rollout checklist.
background: Embeddings traffic is increasingly mixed: interactive UI lookups (low tokens, high QPS, latency-sensitive) and batch async jobs (high throughput, relaxed latency). Current single-envelope SLOs force conservative sizing or overprovisioning. We need a model that preserves predictable latency for priority sessions while allowing lower-priority workloads to consume variable capacity with clear error-budget accounting.
goals: Establish per-session SLO envelopes (latency & availability) for three priority lanes: RealTime, Standard, Bulk
Define asymmetric error-budget burn rules so RealTime tenants are protected during bursts
Specify circuit-breaker thresholds and automated fallback routing to quantized or lower-cost model variants
Create contract tests and synthetic probes to validate SLOs in CI and staging
Design phased rollout gates (canary -> regional -> global) with observability checks
non_goals: Full cost-rebalancing or pricing changes (this ticket only defines SLOs and gates)
Implementing new kernel-level runtime optimizations (covered in ENG roadmap)
Tenant billing reconciliation — out of scope
proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-lane SLO system for embeddings with explicit per-tenant provisional error budgets and asymmetric burn multipliers. RealTime: tight latency envelope and low burn tolerance; Standard: balanced envelope with medium tolerance; Bulk: high throughput allowed with relaxed latency SLO and aggressive burn allowance. Implement automated shunt rules to fallback model variant (quantized/low-cost) when a tenant's burn score exceeds threshold and global capacity signals indicate high contention.
detailed_requirements: SLO definitions (per-lane): p95 and p99 latency targets, availability percentage, and request success rate
Error budget accounting: rolling 7d window and rolling 30d window; formula must support asymmetric burn multipliers per lane
Per-tenant provisional budgets: initial allocation based on historical QPS with override via admin API
Burn score computation: weighted combination of latency violations, error rate, and quota overcommit; RealTime multiplier=0.5, Standard=1.0, Bulk=2.0
Circuit-breaker rules: immediate headroom-based shunt when burn score > 0.9 OR region capacity utilization > 0.85 for > 2 minutes
Fallback routing policy: attempt quantized variant (same model family) with up to 2 parallel attempts before degradation path
Observability hooks: per-tenant SLO dashboards, burn score timeline, probe failure annotation
APIs: admin endpoints to query/override tenant budgets, and a rollout gating API to pause/accelerate progressive release
Contract tests: synthetic probe matrix (small/med/large embedding jobs) targeting p95/p99 and availability thresholds
Documentation: user-facing doc explaining lanes, expected behavior under contention, and how to request upgrades
acceptance_criteria: Definition: SLO document published with numeric targets for each lane and example tenant allocations
Contract tests: CI passes for synthetic probes in staging that demonstrate lanes meeting targets under controlled load (see test_plan)
Automation: circuit-breaker and fallback rules implemented in routing service and exercised by integration test
Observability: dashboard templates created and wired to per-tenant metrics; burn score metric emitted at 1s granularity
Rollout gates: canary checklist (health, burn delta, error budget consumption rate) defined and automated in release pipeline
Stakeholder sign-off: PM, Eng lead, SRE, and a sample customer success rep approve the PRD and acceptance matrix
metrics_and_slos: Error budget math: EB_day = (1 - availability_target) * 86400s; per-request burn = violation_weighted_duration / EB_window_seconds; burn multipliers apply by lane
Burn score threshold for protective action: 0.9 (protective), 1.0 (critical)
Region capacity signal: node_utilization > 85% sustained over 2 minutes triggers regional-protective measures
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy to 5% of traffic, selected tenants across lanes. Run synthetic probes continuously for 48 hours. Gate: no increase in RealTime p99 beyond 10% of baseline and burn rate < 0.2/day
Phase 2 (regional ramp): expand to region-wide 25% traffic. Gate: burn delta < 0.5 and stability for 24 hours
Phase 3 (global ramp): 100% traffic, enable automatic shunt rules. Gate: dashboards show correct per-tenant segmentation and circuit-breaker firing counts within expected range
Rollback criteria: sustained >20% increase in p99 for RealTime over 1 hour, or persistent burn score >1.0 for >30 minutes
Communication: pre-rollout emails to top 50 tenants, and in-console notification about lane semantics
test_plan: Unit tests for burn score calculation and multiplier logic
Integration test that simulates mixed synchronous and asynchronous workloads and validates fallback routing behavior
Staging contract test suite: 3x synthetic probes (small, medium, bulk) run during canary with pass/fail thresholds
Chaos test: simulate node loss in region and verify circuit-breaker triggers and graceful degradation
CI contract: fail PRs that change SLO doc without updating contract tests
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overprotecting RealTime lane could starve Bulk customers and increase costs. Mitigation: set conservative initial provisional budgets and monitor cost impact for two weeks
Risk: burn multipliers mis-calibrated; may lead to false positives. Mitigation: start with conservative multipliers and run A/B calibration experiments in staging
Risk: increased complexity for customers to understand lanes. Mitigation: produce clear UX copy and one-click upgrade path, customer success outreach
Risk: routing oscillation under rapid traffic spikes. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum enforcement windows (e.g., 60s) before automatic shunt toggles
